summary: The Lower Health Care Costs Act extends temporary changes from the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021 and the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 for three additional years, through 2028. These changes expand eligibility for the health care premium tax credit by continuing to remove the maximum income limit and keeping the credit amounts higher through lower applicable percentages.

affected_groups.effect: May continue to claim expanded eligibility and increased amounts for the health care premium tax credit through 2028.
affected_groups.group: Taxpayers obtaining health insurance through health insurance exchanges

affected_groups.effect: Remain eligible for the premium tax credit through 2028 without being barred by the previous maximum income limit.
affected_groups.group: Taxpayers with household incomes exceeding 400 percent of the federal poverty level

key_provisions: Extends the elimination of the 400% federal poverty level maximum income limit for premium tax credit eligibility through the end of 2028.
Extends lower applicable percentages used to calculate the amount of the premium tax credit through 2028.
Extends the pause on adjusting applicable percentages for inflation through 2028.
Applies these extensions to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025.

summary_detail.plain_summary: The Lower Health Care Costs Act extends temporary changes from the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021 and the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 for three additional years, through 2028. These changes expand eligibility for the health care premium tax credit by continuing to remove the maximum income limit and keeping the credit amounts higher through lower applicable percentages.
summary_detail.significance: The bill maintains current temporary health insurance subsidy rules for an additional three years, preventing expansions from expiring at the end of 2025.
